value: Zier, M., Pflugradt, N., Stenzel, P., Kotzur, L. and Stolten, D. (2023). Industrial decarbonization pathways: The example of the German glass industry. Energy Conversion and Management: X, 17, 100336. doi:10.1016/j.ecmx.2022.100336

Locators are printed journal page numbers (1-20); appendix tables are on pp.16-19. A bottom-up emissions model of German container and flat glass; it contains NO capex, opex or measured furnace data (the authors list CAPEX/OPEX as outside scope). Loaded: modelled 2019 fleet-mean melting SEC and CO2, Table 1 scenario SECs and efficiency improvements, Table G2 patterned-glass SEC, Table G3 lifetimes, oxygen electricity. Container-glass SEC by furnace type and pull rate is in Fig. G1 (a chart; values not printed, not loaded). Energy basis is LHV per t glass melted (not packed; pack-to-melt 0.9 container, 0.83 flat). The hybrid option (70% electricity, 30% hydrogen) SECs are derived from the printed 4.4 GJ/t. Hydrogen options have no SEC of their own: same as natural gas (hydrogen) or 30% lower (hydrogen efficient). zier_2021_001 is a different paper (the 2021 review). The paper's CO2 budget and scenario emissions are not technology data and are not loaded.
